summary.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion; reported PBT margin 9.5%, or 11.5% excluding demerger one-offs.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue grew 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion, led by OEM orders from wind, metals and rail. Reported PBT margin recovered to 9.5% from negative 7.8% in Q3, but this includes demerger-related one-offs; excluding them, margin was 11.5% versus 13.1% in Q3. Net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales on lower inventory. Management guided margins back to around 13% after demerger costs end and about 15% by FY29-30, with capex of around INR 800 crore planned through FY30 for a new Pune plant. YoY comparisons were not presented because prior-period figures were extracted from SKF India Limited.

financial_highlights.change: +9.8% QoQ; +31% YoY (as stated by management, on a non-comparable basis)
from -7.8% in Q3 FY26; +1,731 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Profit before tax margin (excl. demerger one-offs)

financial_highlights.value: About INR 1.8 billion (IT, professional services, stamp duty on land transfer)
OEM about 51%, distribution about 35%, exports about 6%, sales to SKF India about 4%, other income about 3%

segments.name: OEM
segments.commentary: OEM share rose to about 50% of Q4 sales from 46%; wind grew 91% QoQ on ZF and Suzlon deliveries, metals grew on Tata Steel and SAIL orders, and rail grew about 12% QoQ. FY26 OEM split: railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy industries 7%, metals 6%.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution fell in Q4, with share dropping to 32% from 38%, as volume shifted away from distributors with overdue payments and some shipments were held back. Management expects this to recover.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports performed well in Q4, mainly to Europe and Southeast Asia; about 6% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Sales to SKF India (automotive)
segments.commentary: Intercompany sales to SKF India Limited were the second-largest growth driver in Q4, linked to automotive demand; about 4% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: Margin (excl. one-offs) expected to return to around 13% by end of calendar 2026 as demerger costs finish and distribution mix recovers.
Long-term target of about 15% PBT margin by FY29-30, with 16-18% as aspiration but not committed.
Net working capital expected at 19-20% of sales going forward.
Growth expected around 8% in the interim until the new Pune plant is operational.
Expect to pass on FX impact and 3-4% cost escalation through price increases; pricing actions already taken with distributors.
capex_capacity: Total capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30, mainly for the new Pune plant and new DGBB and TRB channels.
New Pune plant expected to start operating mid-2028, with full channel transfer and ramp-up complete by end of calendar 2028.
Tapered roller bearing capacity at Pune raised from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces via machine upgrades; cost down about 18%, changeover time down 20%, new product lead time down about 35%.
Until the new plant is ready, SKF India Limited continues job-work manufacturing; additional demand sourced from SKF Ahmedabad and Nilai.
demand_pricing: Industrial production grew about 4.5% YoY; construction grew 6.6% and iron and steel production 9.7%.
Wind is primarily India-driven; India is described as the fastest-growing wind market. Company exited wind and some rail (freight) and tractor business earlier and is re-entering due to localization.
Q4 margin was pressured by OEM mix (lower margin) and higher employee cost from full 100% bonus accrual versus partial payout in Q3.

Other expenses rose on royalty and trademark payments (about INR 60 million higher) and manufacturing costs (repairs, power and fuel, stores). A transfer pricing margin on services from SKF India was also booked.
Competition described as intense, especially at OEMs. Rupee depreciation is a bigger cost headwind than steel and oil-linked inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 segment-wise mix across general machinery, heavy industries, metals, railway, wind, OEM, aftermarket and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26: distribution about 35%, OEM about 51%, exports about 6%, SKF India sales about 4%, other income about 3%. Within OEM: railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy industries 7%, metals 6%.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation trending, how much price has been taken, and how will margins evolve with capacity additions and demerger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin to return to about 13% by end of calendar 2026; about 15% by FY29-30. Cost escalation projected at 3-4%, with FX as the bigger headwind. Pricing actions already taken with distributors; OEM price escalation being negotiated and expected to be harder.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between current margins and the 13-15% historical range, and what drives the path to 16-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drags are extra investments in Pune including the new plant, intense OEM competition, higher railway mix, and higher depreciation. Management targets around 15% through 2030 and says 16-18% is an aspiration that cannot yet be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prioritise growth over margin, given exits and re-entries in wind, rail and tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is growth while maintaining margin, with a target of about 15%. Re-entering wind, freight rail and tractor segments through localization means winning share at lower OEM margins, which management expects to improve through efficiency and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex timeline and when will new capacity be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30. New Pune plant expected to be operational mid-2028, with full ramp-up and channel transfers complete by end of 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 350-400 crore channel expansion investment and how will growth be delivered until the new plant is ready?
qa_highlights.answer: The investment is plant and machinery for DGBB and TRB channels at the new Pune plant, not warehouses. Growth is guided at about 8% in the interim, supported by job-work from SKF India and sourcing from Ahmedabad and Nilai.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the demerger cost roll-off, distribution mix recovery, and price pass-through of FX and 3-4% cost escalation, especially with OEM customers.
Rupee depreciation and steel and oil-linked costs could widen the cost gap.
Heavy intercompany activity with SKF India Limited: sales, transfer pricing margin, royalty and payables/receivables settlement could affect working capital.
Distribution volume was held back due to overdue payments; watch whether distributor volumes recover in the next quarters.
Capex execution on the new Pune plant (mid-2028 start, end-2028 full ramp) and any delays.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sales and working capital, with clear acknowledgement that margins are temporarily depressed by demerger costs and OEM mix. Management was cautious on the 16-18% aspiration and avoided committing beyond about 15% by FY30. Some answers were deflected (e.g., on exact cost line items, which the CFO covered later).
key_quotes: So, we are reporting quarter-on-quarter, which is we are comparing here Q3 of the financial year to Q4 of the financial year.
The OEM business which we are winning, though it comes at a lower margin as you'll see in the subsequent slides, helps us in long-term aftermarket business and that will improve our margin also.

So, our aspiration is to get to 16 % to 18 %, but right now up to 2030, both due to slightly higher OEM mix and a little higher depreciation charges, we see this, we have been conservative here in saying we are going to get to around 15 %.

So, we expect that growth to continue. We are, till that new plant comes up, comes about, we are continuing to do some our SKF India entity is continuing to manufacture some for us on a job work basis.
